entities.name: Gertrude of Nivelles
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gertrude of Nivelles, OSB was an influential abbess who, with her mother Itta, co-founded the Abbey of Nivelles, now in Belgium, in 653.

Established during the early medieval period, the Abbey of Nivelles played a crucial role in the preservation and dissemination of classical knowledge, Christian theology, and monastic practices.

Gertrude's leadership and vision helped to establish the abbey as a center of learning and spirituality, attracting scholars and pilgrims from across Europe.

The abbey's scriptorium, under Gertrude's guidance, produced numerous illuminated manuscripts, including the Historia Ecclesiastica Gentis Anglorum, a chronicle of the history of the English church.

Gertrude's legacy extends beyond the Abbey of Nivelles, as she was venerated in the Catholic and Eastern Orthodox traditions, influencing the development of monasticism and spirituality in Western Europe.
